title: Combinatorial Maximum Flow via Weighted Push-Relabel on Shortcut Graphs
authors: Aaron Bernstein (New York University, New York, USA), Joakim Blikstad (Centrum Wiskunde & Informatica, Amsterdam, Netherlands), Jason Li (Carnegie Mellon University, Pittsburgh, USA), Thatchaphol Saranurak (University of Michigan, Ann Arbor, USA), Ta-Wei Tu (Stanford University, Stanford, USA)
abstract: We give a combinatorial algorithm for computing exact maximum flows in directed graphs with n vertices and edge capacities from {1,…,U} in Õ(n^{2}\log U) time, which is near-optimal on dense graphs. This shaves an n^{o(1)} factor from the recent result of [Bernstein-Blikstad-Saranurak-Tu FOCS'24] and, more importantly, greatly simplifies their algorithm. We believe that ours is by a significant margin the simplest of all algorithms that go beyond Õ(m√n) time in general graphs. To highlight this relative simplicity, we provide a full implementation of the algorithm in C++. The only randomized component of our work is the cut-matching game. Via existing tools, we show how to derandomize it for vertex-capacitated max flow and obtain a deterministic Õ(n^2) time algorithm. This marks the first deterministic near-linear time algorithm for this problem (or even for the special case of bipartite matching) in any density regime.
